said.text: These bills give the NYPD too much power to police speech, and raise serious constitutional concerns. … Because schools and houses of worship are located across the city, these police-controlled zones risk broadly limiting constitutionally protected protest, advocacy, and dissent.

did.text: Voted No on Int 0929-2026, requiring a transparency report on NYPD security perimeters adjacent to educational facilities. Passed 39–10.

whyNote: Council Member Hanif's March stated remarks opposed Int 1-B and Int 175-B, the bills that created the security-perimeter framework; in June she voted No on Int 929-A, a related measure requiring reports on those perimeters. The statement concerns the underlying framework rather than the reporting bill itself; her stated reason for this specific vote was not located. Full remarks are at the source link.
